findings.text: Overflow reporting exposes add, subtract and multiply handlers that forward caller supplied metadata plus two operand references to a shared routine with an operator tag distinguishing the three cases. The shared routine suppresses repeats, selects signed versus unsigned wording from the type record, renders both operands, and emits a representability diagnostic naming the destination type.

Additional arithmetic handlers cover unary negation, division remainder, and implicit conversion. Negation reports a single operand that cannot be represented after sign flip. Division distinguishes a negative one divisor for signed types from a zero divisor case, rendering the dividend. Conversion renders source and destination values and names source type, check flavor and destination type plus truncated outcome.

Memory safety handlers cover type mismatch in two metadata versions, array index range, and shift bounds. Both mismatch versions normalize to a common record with location, type, alignment and check flavor before dispatch. Out of bounds renders the index and names the array type. Shift handling evaluates negative exponent, oversized exponent, negative shifted value and unrepresentable outcome in that priority.

Remaining handlers cover unreachable execution, loading a value invalid for its type, and failed alignment promises. Unreachable logs then terminates execution without return. Invalid load renders the offending value and names its expected type. Alignment handling reports promised stride with optional offset, then derives actual stride from the lowest set bit and residual misalignment of the adjusted address.

Reporting is suppressed when the current context is already inside sanitizer handling or when the location has been reported before. The once-only marker shares storage with line and column and is set atomically on first use, so only the first hit at a site produces output and recursive entry is avoided.

Integer recognition rests on a kind field. For integers the low info bit records signedness and the upper info bits encode base two logarithm of width, so width is recovered by shifting one by half the info value. A type fits inline when its width does not exceed the width of an unsigned machine word, with an internal consistency check that the examined type is integer.

Value helpers sign extend inline words by shifting out and back the surplus high bits, read wider values from memory by width, and test negativity only for signed types. Rendering prints narrow signed values as decimal signed, narrow unsigned as decimal unsigned, and the widest width as grouped hexadecimal; wide rendering is only available where the target advertises very wide integer support.

A type record holds a kind code, an info field packing signedness and size, and a trailing variable length name. A location record holds a file name pointer plus a union that either tracks whether the site already reported or stores line and column numbers as a pair.

Arithmetic and call metadata records pair a location with type references and operation specific items. Overflow keeps one type. Conversion keeps source and destination types plus a check flavor. Range records keep array and index types for indexing or two operand types for shifts. Unreachable keeps only a location, invalid load keeps location plus type, alignment keeps two locations plus type, and nonnull argument keeps two locations plus an argument position.

Mismatch metadata exists in current and legacy shapes plus a normalized common shape used for dispatch. Current form stores full alignment, legacy stores logarithmic alignment later expanded by shifting, and both store location, type and check flavor. The common form references location by pointer and carries resolved alignment, allowing one dispatch routine to serve both versions.
A fixed buffer extent of 40 bytes is reserved for rendering single operand strings in diagnostics, used for left, right, old, from, to and index spellings.

A check enumeration names about two dozen sanitizer conditions spanning arithmetic overflow, unreachable execution, control flow and type checks, conversions, invalid values, nullability, bounds, shifts and alignment promises. A separate small kind enumeration distinguishes integer from floating point with zero and one, and reserves all ones in sixteen bits for unknown.
Wide integer aliases have two configurations: a very wide signed and unsigned pair when the toolchain offers them, otherwise sixty four bit signed and unsigned fallbacks.
Header uses a conventional include guard macro to prevent double inclusion.
A linkage helper expands to an architecture calling convention marker on configurations that need it and to nothing elsewhere, letting sanitizer handlers share one declaration across targets.

Sixty four bit unsigned comparison splits each operand into high and low halves and orders by high half first then low half. It returns zero when the first is smaller, two when larger, and one when equal, and is marked to avoid tracing.

Two byte character length helpers count units until a zero unit or a caller limit, with unbounded length implemented as bounded length with the largest limit. Byte size helpers scale the bounded count by unit size and treat the caller limit as a byte budget converted to units.

Bounded copy requires a nonzero room and rejects absurdly large room with a too big error. It copies unit by unit, returning the count before the terminator when one fits, otherwise forcing termination at the last slot and signalling truncation with the same too big error. Bounded compare orders lexicographically, returning negative, positive or zero, and stops early on length exhaustion or joint termination.

UTF eight sizing charges one byte for values below one hundred twenty eight, two below two thousand forty eight, and three otherwise. Transcoding writes one to three byte sequences with standard leading and continuation markers, respects an output budget by stopping before an incomplete sequence, terminates when room remains, and returns bytes written excluding termination.

Set membership finds the representative by climbing parent links while halving the path so each visited node skips one level. Union attaches the lower rank tree beneath the higher rank tree, and when ranks tie attaches one root beneath the other and increments the survivor rank; already unified inputs are left unchanged.
User copy shims forward direction, addresses and length to inline implementations and return the residual uncopied count, preserving the conventional nonzero on short copy contract.

Zero verification of user memory treats empty input as verified, aligns the start down to word boundary while masking ignored leading bytes, then scans word by word and masks ignored trailing bytes. It returns one for all zero, zero on first nonzero, and a fault code when the user range cannot be entered or read, always closing the access window before returning.

Null universally unique and globally unique identifiers exist as zero filled constants. One index table is identity across sixteen octets while the companion swaps byte order within the first three fields and leaves the tail identity, capturing endian differences between the two textual layouts.

Random identifier creation fills sixteen octets from the randomness source then stamps variant bits in octet index eight to select the standard variant. Universally unique stamping puts version four in octet index six while globally unique stamping puts version four in octet index seven, reflecting differing field layouts; a shared helper handles randomness plus variant and thin wrappers add version.

Textual parsing first validates the canonical hyphenated spelling then converts sixteen hex pairs at skipping hyphen offsets into bytes permuted through the caller supplied index table, returning zero on success and an invalid argument code on malformed input. Dedicated wrappers supply the universally unique versus globally unique permutation.

Formatted output control keeps a post init immutable flag deciding whether pointer values are shown and an init time policy selecting automatic, always hash or never hash behavior. A decimal table holds one hundred precomputed two character codes used to accelerate number rendering.
Unbounded signed string to integer conversion delegates to a bounded worker with the largest integer limit, propagating end pointer and base handling.

Each reporting site follows suppression test, prologue that marks entry and logs tag with reason and file plus masked line and column and notifies test harness, emission of case specific detail, then epilogue that dumps call stack, closes the trace marker, clears the entry mark and evaluates warn to panic escalation.

Mismatch handling saves the user access state, then selects null dereference for zero address, misaligned access when required alignment is nonzero and address fails it, otherwise object size mismatch, and finally restores the saved access state. Shift and invalid load handlers follow the same save and restore pairing with early restore on suppressed sites.

No sleeping locks are taken in the shown paths. Mutual exclusion relies on an atomic once bit per location for single reporting and a per context nesting counter incremented on entry and decremented on exit to block recursion. User memory access windows are strictly paired save and restore around reads that may touch user addresses.

The unreachable handler does not return because it terminates the system after logging, so callers must not assume continuation. Wide value rendering depends on very wide integer support and otherwise triggers an internal warning path without producing output. Alignment diagnostics compute a mask from promised stride minus one and therefore assume a nonzero promise.

Bounded two byte copy truncates to room minus one with forced termination and reports too big rather than silent shortening. Zero checking and shift plus invalid load paths can observe user faults and must propagate fault codes or skip output while still restoring access state. Shift diagnostics prioritize negative exponent over oversized exponent over negative value, so combined violations report only the first.
